sources.title: Talorys – A self-hosted personal AI agent on Cloudflare's free tier

editorial.how: According to the documentation: "The browser only ever talks to your .pages.dev site. /api/ requests run a Pages Function that forwards them over a service binding to the agent Worker. The agent Worker is deployed with workersdev: false and previewurls: false: it has no public URL. Authentication and authorization happen in the Worker, not the frontend. Chat responses stream as Server-Sent Events end-to-end."
editorial.why: The GitHub API reports 1.5k stars and 147 forks, 33 days after the repository was created. It gained 23 stars across 165 hours of our snapshots. Primary language: TypeScript.
editorial.what: Your personal AI agent in your own Cloudflare account. Chat, memory, tasks, notes and scheduled reminders, deployed with one command: npx create-talorys@latest. Free-tier friendly, single-user, no telemetry. From the documentation: "Talorys is a free, open-source personal AI assistant that runs entirely inside your own Cloudflare account. It chats with you, remembers what matters, manages tasks, notes and projects, and runs reminders and routines on a schedule — without any server, database or account operated by the Talorys developers."
editorial.whoCares: Developers building or operating agents that use tools, browsers or computers.
limitations: One independent reference so far: Hacker News.

editorial.why: Lobsters thread: 325 points, 273 comments.
editorial.what: The vibecoding tag has been getting more and more useless for a while now. It lost the original meaning as the culture of software engineering with LLMs matured a bit. It got silly when posts talking about LLMs in general got tagged. It got useless when posts even mentioning some project created with LLMs in passing got tagged. Now it actually got harmful to the community when tagging posts turns away very valuable…
